correctness.rationale: For an unselected vertex the open signature is the selected opposite shore with its matched index removed. Two outside vertices on the same shore collide exactly when both their partners are omitted; across shores nonempty signatures cannot collide. Thus at most one pair is wholly omitted, and domination requires separate checks only for empty or singleton selected shores. These conditions give the three nonempty pair weights x, y, xy and the four boundary subtractions (counting symmetries); only at n=3 do singleton-shore defects overlap, in six words. At degree n-1 there is one omitted pair, all other pairs singly selected, and each selected shore must contain at least two vertices, giving the specified bidegree counts for n≥5. For n=3 and 4 this layer vanishes and degree n has coefficients 14 and 56, respectively. In the complete biclique twin classes force at most one omission on each shore, and one omission per shore is attainable. An independent direct-adjacency enumeration checked every joint coefficient at n=3 through 8 and the biclique minimum; it agrees, including the exceptional and minimum layers.
residual_risks: The exhaustive finite check covers only n=3 through 8; the general conclusion uses the combinatorial proof. No claim for n=2 or for predicates concerning all vertices.

value.rationale: A full two-shore enumerator is a useful invariant, and the matching deletion is a natural comparison showing sensitivity of location-domination. As a contribution of this frozen record, however, those results are already determined by the earlier exact and equivalent classifications; the only reformulation is to divide two known minima to state the factor two. There is no substantive new exact invariant or deletion theorem to retain.
residual_risks: This is a judgment on the contribution of this record, not on the utility of the underlying counts or on arbitrary patterns of edge deletion.
